problem: Both plotted curves peak at 1.0 at x = 5. The curve named 'small SD' (exp(-((x-5)²)/1.0)) is narrower but is below the 'large SD' curve everywhere except at the peak. The caption and aria call the smaller-SD curve 'taller'/'tall', which contradicts the plot a student sees. A student gets the wrong picture of how a smaller SD changes a frequency curve.
fix: Normalise both curves so the smaller-SD curve is taller, e.g. y = exp(-((x-5)²)/(2σ²))/(σ√(2π)) with σ ≈ 0.707 for 'small SD' and σ ≈ 1.414 for 'large SD', and set the y-axis maximum near 0.6. Alternatively remove 'taller'/'tall' and 'short' from the caption and aria and describe only the width.

problem: 'Use absolute distances, because signed distances cancel to zero' is exactly true only when the centre A is the mean. For the median the signed deviations do not sum to zero, so the stated reason is incomplete and can confuse a student who chooses the median.
fix: Say: 'Use absolute distances, because signed deviations from the mean add to zero, and in any case positive and negative deviations would cancel each other.'
